# A joint cap/chord inequality for an actual triangle

This is an ordinary planar theorem. It retains all three actual cap
normals and the actual triangle vertices. It makes no assertion about
compatibility of distinct mixed-integer fibers or a global OC bound.

## 1. Statement

Let K be a triangle, y an interior point, and let three nonzero spanning
normals v_1,v_2,v_3 satisfy v_1+v_2+v_3=0. Suppose each cap through y
captures exactly one strict vertex of K, these three vertices are
distinct, and neither of its other vertices lies on its boundary.
Label the captured vertex P_i. Put

    q_i=|K intersect {v_i.(x-y)>=0}|/|K|,
    sigma_i=H_1(K intersect {v_i.(x-y)=0})/||v_i||,
    lambda_i=(1/sigma_i)/sum_j(1/sigma_j).

Define positive normalized heights a_i and positive off-diagonal
values b_ij by dividing all the following quantities by the same
positive number sum_i v_i.(P_i-y):

    a_i=v_i.(P_i-y),           b_ij=-v_i.(P_j-y), i!=j.

Thus sum_i a_i=1. The normal balance gives the column identities

    sum_(i!=j)b_ij=a_j.                                      (1)

Let

    f_i=2a_i/sqrt(q_i)>0.

**Theorem.** These data satisfy

    sum_i f_i sqrt(q_i)=2,
    f_i+(f_j+f_k)^2/4<=2             for {i,j,k}={1,2,3}.     (2)

Equivalently, putting Q=sum_i lambda_i q_i, the inequalities are

    2lambda_i sqrt(q_i)Q
       +(lambda_j sqrt(q_j)+lambda_k sqrt(q_k))^2<=2Q^2.     (3)

The hypotheses on incidence follow, for example, from the cap ceiling
q_i<=128/279 by the independently proved sharp incidence theorem
`candidate ca9f00bdb64d6d9e`.

## 2. Exact signed-row proof

Use cyclic indices and define

    s_i=b_i,i+1+b_i,i+2,
    d_i=b_i,i+1-b_i,i+2,
    g_i=2a_i+s_i.

Equation (1) gives sum_i s_i=1, sum_i g_i=3, and, with this orientation,

    g_i=1-d_(i+1)+d_(i+2).                                 (4)

For example, 2a_1=s_2-d_2+s_3+d_3, and adding s_1 proves the
formula for g_1. Each g_i>|d_i| because a_i>0 and s_i>=|d_i|.

The two edge-intercept fractions of the corner cap at P_i give

    q_i=a_i^2/[(a_i+b_i,i+1)(a_i+b_i,i+2)].                  (5)

It follows exactly that

    f_i^2=4(a_i+b_i,i+1)(a_i+b_i,i+2)=g_i^2-d_i^2.         (6)

We use the following elementary inequality. If G>|u| and H>|v|,
then

    sqrt(G^2-u^2)+sqrt(H^2-v^2)
        <=sqrt((G+H)^2-(u+v)^2).                          (7)

Indeed GH-uv>0 and

    (GH-uv)^2-(G^2-u^2)(H^2-v^2)=(Gv-Hu)^2>=0.

Squaring the two sides of (7) therefore proves it; all square roots
are real and nonnegative. This is often called the reverse triangle
inequality on the two-dimensional future Lorentz cone, but the displayed
algebra is a complete proof here.

For fixed i, apply (7) to (g_j,d_j) and (g_k,-d_k). By (4),

    g_j+g_k=3-g_i,       (d_j-d_k)^2=(1-g_i)^2.

Consequently

    f_j+f_k<=sqrt((3-g_i)^2-(1-g_i)^2)=2sqrt(2-g_i).        (8)

In particular g_i<2, since the left side is positive. Also f_i<=g_i
by (6). Combining these inequalities gives (2). Its linear identity
is immediate from sum_i a_i=1.

Finally the actual corner-cap area is sigma_i times its unnormalized
vertex height divided by two. Hence lambda_i is proportional to
a_i/q_i. Normalizing sum a_i=1 gives a_i=lambda_i q_i/Q, and therefore
f_i=2lambda_i sqrt(q_i)/Q. Substitution proves (3).

## 3. An exact nonnegative deficit and its equality cases

The target-i deficit in (2) has the exact decomposition

    2-f_i-(f_j+f_k)^2/4
      =d_i^2/(g_i+f_i)
       +(g_j d_k+g_k d_j)^2
          /[2(g_j g_k+d_j d_k+f_j f_k)].                 (9)

Both denominators are strictly positive. To verify the identity, use
g_i-f_i=d_i^2/(g_i+f_i), and note that the difference between the
square of the right side of (8) and (f_j+f_k)^2 equals
2(g_j g_k+d_j d_k-f_j f_k). Rationalizing that last difference uses

    (g_j g_k+d_j d_k)^2-f_j^2 f_k^2
       =(g_j d_k+g_k d_j)^2.

Thus the inequality is joint across the actual three rows, and its
loss is an explicit sum of two nonnegative quantities.

Equality for index i holds exactly when

    d_i=0,                 d_j+d_k=0.                    (10)

For necessity, (9) first gives d_i=0. Equations (4) then show

    g_j d_k+g_k d_j=(d_j+d_k)(2-g_i).

The second factor is positive by (8), proving the second equality.
Conversely (10) makes both squares in (9) zero. In particular equality
forces g_j=g_k and f_j=f_k. It does not by itself force q_j=q_k or
a_j=a_k. Any such further symmetry would require a separate argument.

## 4. A useful one-coordinate elimination

Write t=sqrt(q_1), r=sqrt(q_2), s=sqrt(q_3), x=f_1, and
Y=2-xt. The identity in (2) gives Y=r f_2+s f_3. Therefore

    Z:=f_2/r+f_3/s=[(r+s)(f_2+f_3)-Y]/(rs).

Using only the first inequality in (2),

    Z<=[2(r+s)sqrt(2-x)-2+xt]/(rs).                       (11)

Thus a sufficient scalar inequality for lambda_1>=2/9 is

    x(7rs-2t^2)+4t>=4t(r+s)sqrt(2-x).                   (12)

It remains necessary to impose the moment identity, nonnegative f_i,
the other two inequalities (2), the individual cap ceiling, and the
full sorted cap profile when investigating whether (12) follows.
The next section proves the needed implication using a symmetric
relaxation of the cap profile. The exact deficit (9) additionally imposes
actual equality restrictions beyond the three inequalities alone.

## 5. A scalar closure with exact constants

The following proposition supplies the implication that was left open
in Section 4, under a symmetric relaxation of the full cap profile.

**Proposition.** Set

    c=128/279,       q_0=119/279,       C=125/93,
    m=sqrt(20/49),   s=sqrt(c),        rho=sqrt(q_0).

Suppose q_i and f_i are positive numbers satisfying

    20/49<=q_i<=c,          sum_i q_i<=C,
    sum_i f_i sqrt(q_i)=2,
    f_i+(f_j+f_k)^2/4<=2       for every i.                 (13)

Then every normalized inverse quantity

    (f_i/sqrt(q_i))/sum_j(f_j/sqrt(q_j))

is strictly greater than 2/9.

**Proof.** Suppose the contrary for index 1. Write

    x=f_1, t=sqrt(q_1), g=f_2+f_3, F=x+g.

Summing the three quadratic inequalities in (13) gives

    F+(F^2+sum_i f_i^2)/4<=6.

Since sum_i f_i^2>=F^2/3, this implies F<=3. The moment identity and
q_i<=c give F>=2/s. In fact

    F>=2/s>59/20,                                         (14)

because 4/c-(59/20)^2=13/800>0.

The inverse quantity for index 1 is at least xm/(sF), since its
numerator is at least x/s and its full denominator is at most F/m.
The supposed bound at most 2/9 therefore gives

    x<71/100,                                            (15)

because x<=2s/(3m) and
(71/100)^2-(4/9)(c/(20/49))=113951/25110000>0.

We first show that both f_2 and f_3 are greater than (s/rho)x.
The ratio s/rho=sqrt(128/119) is less than 26/25. If, for example,
f_2<=(s/rho)x, then by (15)

    T:=x+f_2< (51/25)(71/100)=3621/2500<29/20.

The third inequality in (13) gives F<=T+2-T^2/4. This expression
increases for 0<T<2, so

    F<4679/1600<59/20,

contradicting (14). The argument for f_3 is identical. Hence

    f_j/s>x/rho                 for j=2,3.                (16)

Apply the concave square-root tangent inequality at q_0 for q_1 and
at c for q_2,q_3. The latter two coordinate differences are nonpositive.
Thus (16) gives

    2=sum_i f_i sqrt(q_i)
      <=x rho+g s
         +[x/(2rho)](q_1-q_0)
         +sum_(j=2,3)[f_j/(2s)](q_j-c)
      <=x rho+g s+[x/(2rho)](sum_i q_i-q_0-2c)
      <=x rho+g s.                                       (17)

Here q_0+2c=C exactly. The first inequality in (13) supplies
g<=2sqrt(2-x), so

    2<=x rho+2s sqrt(2-x).                                (18)

The function on the right is increasing for 0<x<=71/100. Its derivative
is rho-s/sqrt(2-x)>0, since

    (129/100)q_0-c=2551/27900>0.

At x=67/100 it is strictly smaller than 2. For a wholly rational check,

    rho<65309/100000,
    s<33867/50000,
    sqrt(133/100)<57663/50000.

Each follows by squaring positive quantities; the corresponding square
gaps are, respectively,

    9069199/2790000000000,
    5659231/697500000000,
    21569/2500000000.

With these upper bounds, the gap from 2 is still at least
10269/78125000>0. Equation (18) consequently implies

    67/100<x<71/100.                                      (19)

For every r in [m,s], the elementary secant bound

    1/r<=(m+s-r)/(ms)                                    (20)

holds: after multiplication by rms, its nonnegative difference is
(r-m)(s-r). Let Z=f_2/sqrt(q_2)+f_3/sqrt(q_3). Using the moment identity,
(20), g<=2sqrt(2-x), and t<=s in that order gives

    Z<=[(m+s)g-2+xt]/(ms)
      <=[2(m+s)sqrt(2-x)-2+xs]/(ms).                      (21)

Define

    G(x)=4+x(7m-2s)-4(m+s)sqrt(2-x).

It is strictly increasing for 0<x<2, because 7m-2s>0 and
G'(x)=7m-2s+2(m+s)/sqrt(2-x). Moreover G(67/100)>0.
For an exact rational certificate, use

    m>63887/100000,
    s<33867/50000,
    sqrt(133/100)<57663/50000.

The first lower bound follows from
20/49-(63887/100000)^2=4110319/490000000000>0.
At x=67/100 the coefficient 7x-4sqrt(2-x) of m is positive, even
after the displayed upper bound on the square root. Substituting these
three bounds therefore gives

    G(67/100)>165384/9765625>0.                           (22)

By (19), G(x)>0. Rearranging this inequality and using (21),

    Z<(7/2)x/s<=(7/2)x/t.

This makes (x/t)/(x/t+Z)>2/9, the required contradiction. Notice that
this argument does not multiply by a potentially signed numerator:
the two successive bounds in (21) are valid directly. QED.

## 6. The actual triangle inverse-chord theorem

**Theorem.** Let K be any planar triangle, y an interior point, and
v_1,v_2,v_3 nonzero spanning normals whose sum is zero. Let q_i be their
three cap fractions through y, and sigma_i their normalized chord
lengths. If

    q_i<=128/279        for all i,
    q_min+q_mid+q_max/4<=1,                               (23)

then

    min_i (1/sigma_i)/sum_j(1/sigma_j)>2/9.                (24)

**Proof.** The sharp triangle incidence theorem cited in Section 1
applies because 128/279<2sqrt(3)-3. Thus each cap isolates one distinct
strict vertex, and the signed-row construction and inequalities (2)
are valid.

For completeness, the rational lower cap bound needed in Proposition 5
comes from actual source barycentric coordinates alpha_i. First all
alpha_i<1/2. If alpha_1>=1/2, a cap at vertex 2 with edge-intercept
fractions r,u satisfies alpha_1/r+alpha_3/u=1. Its fraction is
alpha_3 r^2/(r-alpha_1), decreasing for r<=1<=2alpha_1. Consequently
q_2>=alpha_3/(1-alpha_1), and similarly
q_3>=alpha_2/(1-alpha_1); their sum is at least 1, contradicting
q_2,q_3<=128/279<1/2.

The same edge-intercept identity and arithmetic-geometric mean give
q_i>=4alpha_j alpha_k. If z=max alpha_i, then z>=1/3, z<1/2, and
one other coordinate is at least (1-z)/2. Hence 2z(1-z)<=128/279,
so z<5/14, using 23/279>4/49. Any two source coordinates have sum
greater than 9/14 and are each smaller than 5/14. Expanding
(5/14-alpha_j)(5/14-alpha_k)>0 shows alpha_j alpha_k>5/49. Therefore

    q_i>20/49.

The sorted profile (23) gives sum_i q_i<=1+(3/4)(128/279)=125/93.
All scalar hypotheses (13) now hold. Finally the corner-cap height and
section identity in Section 2 gives lambda_i proportional to f_i/sqrt(q_i).
Proposition 5 proves (24).

This theorem is an ordinary triangle statement for the three specified
caps. It does not identify these weights with mixed weights containing
additional endpoint sections, and it does not prove an inverse-chord
bound for a nontriangular body. It requires neither a symmetric triangle
nor a centroid source. No numerical minimizer or existence of a global
optimizer is used in the proof.

## 7. A quantitative strengthening after the independent closure audit

The scalar proposition in Section 5, and hence the actual triangle
theorem in Section 6, admit the explicit stronger conclusion

    min_i lambda_i>223/1000=2/9+7/9000.                   (25)

Here is a complete check of the changes to the already proved argument.
Suppose instead that the first inverse quantity is at most
theta=223/1000. The bound lambda_1>=xm/(sF), with F<=3, now gives
x<=3s theta/m<71/100, since

    (71/100)^2-9theta^2(c/(20/49))=40107/38750000>0.

Every argument from (14) through (19) is therefore unchanged: the
water-filling tangent proof uses only x<71/100, and still proves
67/100<x<71/100. The reciprocal secant estimate (21) is unchanged.

Replace G by

    G_theta(x)=4+x[(2/theta-2)m-2s]
                    -4(m+s)sqrt(2-x).

Its derivative is positive, because 2/theta-2=1554/223 and
(1554/223)m-2s>0. At x=67/100 the same rational lower and upper bounds
used in (22) give

    (1554/223)(67/100)-4(57663/50000)
         =155901/2787500>0,
    G_theta(67/100)>975345521/278750000000>0.              (26)

Thus G_theta(x)>0. Rearranging (26) and (21) yields

    Z<(1/theta-1)x/s<=(1/theta-1)x/t,

so (x/t)/(x/t+Z)>theta, contradicting the supposed bound. This proves
(25), without numerical optimization or any additional geometric
assumption. The quantitative margin is ordinary: transferring it to
weights 1/(sigma_Ki+2sigma_Ai) requires further actual endpoint data.
